response.message:
I've drawn your authenticated assistant on IBM Cloud with real services. Users sign in through App ID, and the app runs on Code Engine. Each user's conversations are stored in Cloudant, answers come from watsonx.ai, and escalations go to a human through an Event Streams topic. Context limits and the model-outage fallback live inside the app, not in separate services. The board doesn't yet prove that these services work together, that a region is available or that your account has access. Nothing is deployed.

For the first local test, we'd swap watsonx.ai for a scripted fake model. That lets us check your five acceptance criteria: one user can't open another user's chats, context and replies stay within size limits, a simulated model outage gives a response the user can recover from, deleting a chat removes its stored context, and escalation keeps only the approved context. A fake model can't show answer quality, real model access, quotas or speed, so those need a separate test against a real watsonx.ai model in your IBM account.

The design is AI-generated, not checked for compatibility. The current export only generates infrastructure code (Terraform) for IBM object storage, so every other part of this design will need engineering work.

Which country must the synthetic conversations stay in?

proposal.title: IBM Cloud authenticated conversational assistant (first sketch)
proposal.body: Scope: an authenticated chat app for synthetic users with per-user conversation storage, a watsonx.ai model, bounded context and a human escalation path. It takes no external actions. Assumptions: the region is not selected, and nothing has been verified for interoperability, model access or account entitlements. Context limits, ownership checks and the outage fallback are modules inside the Code Engine app, not separate deployments. This export has no native Terraform for these components, so they need engineering work.

data.label: Synthetic user (browser)
data.description: Synthetic test user using a browser. A client reference outside the provisioning scope.

data.label: Sign-in
data.description: Handles user sign-in with OIDC authorization code and PKCE, then issues the tokens that the app validates. Uses synthetic user accounts only.

data.label: Assistant application
data.description: Hosts the web UI and chat API. Validates App ID tokens and enforces conversation ownership by token subject. Bounds context with a size limit and trims older turns, and caps response length. If the model times out or is unavailable, returns a recoverable 'try again' response without losing the stored conversation. Deleting a conversation removes its stored context. Escalation sends only the context the user approved. Takes no external actions.

data.label: Conversation state
data.description: Per-user conversation documents, partitioned by user subject. The app is the only writer. Delete removes the conversation documents; backup and retention behaviour must be confirmed.

data.label: Model runtime
data.description: Foundation model inference with a bounded number of input and output tokens. The model, region availability and project access still need to be chosen and verified. Mocked in the local test.

data.label: Escalation queue
data.description: Topic carrying escalation records that contain only the approved conversation context.

data.label: Human support agent
data.description: Person who handles escalated conversations. The review tool is still to be decided.

data.label: Secrets
data.description: Stores API keys and credentials for Cloudant, watsonx.ai and Event Streams. Credentials never appear in the diagram.

data.label: Logs and audit
data.description: Application logs and audit events, without conversation content. Tracks model failures and denied cross-user requests.

requirementDrafts.rationale: Stops one user's conversation data leaking to another user.
requirementDrafts.basis: User acceptance criterion: 'One user cannot read another conversation'.
requirementDrafts.statement: A signed-in user can read, change or delete only conversations they own. Requests for another user's conversation are denied and logged.

requirementDrafts.rationale: Keeps cost, latency and token overruns under control.
requirementDrafts.basis: User acceptance criterion: 'Context and response sizes are bounded'.
requirementDrafts.statement: Context sent to the model and generated responses stay within configured size limits. Older turns are trimmed deterministically.

requirementDrafts.rationale: Prevents a model failure from losing data or crashing the app.
requirementDrafts.basis: User acceptance criterion: 'Model outage produces a recoverable response'.
requirementDrafts.statement: If the model is unavailable or times out, the user gets a recoverable response and the stored conversation is kept.

requirementDrafts.rationale: Gives users control over their data and supports privacy obligations.
requirementDrafts.basis: User acceptance criterion: 'Deleting a conversation removes its stored context'.
requirementDrafts.statement: Deleting a conversation removes its stored context from conversation storage. Backup and retention behaviour is still to be confirmed.

requirementDrafts.rationale: Gives the human agent enough context to help without exposing unapproved data.
requirementDrafts.basis: User acceptance criterion: 'Escalation retains the approved conversation context'.
requirementDrafts.statement: Escalation sends a human agent the approved conversation context and nothing more.
